memory_candidates.content: When extracting a shared helper library out of a mutual duplicate-block pair, extracting only the validation/logging preamble (the smallest, lowest-risk shared surface) can land a net-POSITIVE line count with no later phase queued to absorb/pay it back -- unlike a precedent extraction with further migrations queued, a one-off pair has nowhere for that positive net to go. Check git diff --numstat immediately after the first extraction attempt; if positive and there is no follow-on migration phase to justify carrying it forward, widen the extraction to the actual LARGER duplicate mass (often repeated loop/control-flow bodies, not just the header) before committing, rather than accepting or reverting.

When extracting parallel loop bodies (e.g. install vs. remove, or N near-identical per-type handlers) into one generic parameterized helper, explicitly audit for PRE-EXISTING behavioral discrepancies between the copies before unifying them -- e.g. one copy may skip a validation check the others perform. Preserve the discrepancy via an explicit per-call-site parameter rather than silently normalizing to the stricter (or looser) behavior, since normalizing is an observable behavior change the extraction itself was not chartered to make. A characterization test written before the extraction is what surfaces these discrepancies safely.

git-commit-phase.sh's Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check has a recurring double-slash bug: when a file_scope entry already ends in a trailing slash (e.g. 'agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/'), the containment test appends '/*' to form 'tests//*', which never matches a real single-slash descendant path, causing legitimate in-scope files to be dropped from the phase-closing commit. This has now hit three consecutive phases in the same task. Recovery: a follow-up commit via git-commit-scoped.sh (called directly, bypassing the buggy wrapper) naming exactly the dropped paths -- never widen the phase commit's pathspec to work around it. The underlying fix (strip a trailing '/' from the file_scope entry before appending '/*' in is_contained()) has not yet been applied upstream.
